Flood Insurance Data

Building deductibles on record: NFIP single-family homes by county

In plain words

15.1% of NFIP (federal flood insurance) policies on single-family primary homes with a known building deductible, in force on August 31, 2026, have a building deductible on record of $5,000 or more. In the median listed county it is 21.5%.

Find your county. 1,793 counties are listed. A county with fewer than 30 of these policies is not listed.

FEMA's records hold 2,312,971 single-family primary-home policy units with a known building deductible in force on the data date, across all U.S. counties. In the 1,793 counties with at least 30 of these policies, 15.0% had a building deductible of $5,000 or more on record (90% range 13.2–17.0%, resampling counties).

By Michael Woo, publisher of Flood Insurance Data (about the site), who works with data, is not an insurance agent, adjuster or engineer, and answers for every figure here. Written with AI tools; every row is recomputed from FEMA's records by a separate check before publishing. First published 2026-11-13; data as of August 31, 2026.

Abstract

Data: 1,793 counties with at least 30 single-family primary-home policy units with a known building deductible each (2,300,276 in all), from FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP Policies v3, policies in force, as of August 31, 2026.

Result: The median county's share is 21.5%; the highest is Marengo County, AL at 67.9% (36 of 53), and the lowest share, 0.0%, is shared by 6 counties.

Question

In which U.S. counties do single-family primary homes insured by the NFIP most often have a building deductible of $5,000 or more on record? The measure is the share of single-family primary-home NFIP policy units in force whose building deductible is $5,000 or more.

FEMA defines buildingDeductibleCode as "The total deductible amount in dollars for buildings, both main and appurtenant, that can be applied against the loss."

The FEMA codes counted as $5,000 or more, in the data dictionary's own form: 5 - $5,000, A - $10,000, B - $15,000, C - $20,000, D - $25,000, E - $50,000. FEMA's standard codes below $5,000, counted in the base but not the share: 0 - $500, 9 - $750, 1 - $1,000, F - $1,250, G - $1,500, 2 - $2,000, 3 - $3,000, 4 - $4,000.

Data

FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP Policies v3 (API) records as of August 31, 2026, FEMA fields buildingDeductibleCode, policyCount, occupancyType, primaryResidenceIndicator, condominiumCoverageTypeCode, censusGeoid. Base: NFIP policies in force on the data date on single-family primary homes (FEMA occupancy type 1 or 11, primary residence, not a condominium coverage type), counted as policy units (sum of policyCount). Every such record here holds one unit, which the check confirms. Units with a blank building deductible code are left out, as are codes outside FEMA's standard list, such as H (used only for Group Flood Insurance Policies).

FEMA defines policyCount as "Insured units in an active status."

Methods

A county's share is how many of these policies had a building deductible of $5,000 or more on record, out of all of these policies in the county FEMA codes on the record, both counted from the same records. Left out: 1,139 counties with fewer than 30 of these policies and 95 with none. In the 1,139 left-out counties with at least one, the median share of building deductibles of $5,000 or more is 21.4% and the pooled share 24.6%, so the listed counties are not a sample of every county. Intervals, fifths, the county-resampling range, records left out and why no test is run: shared methods for every paper.

Results

  • Pooled over the 1,793 counties: 15.0% (90% range 13.2–17.0%) of 2,300,276 single-family primary-home policy units with a known building deductible; the 1,139 counties left out pool to 24.6%.
  • Median county: 21.5%. Highest: Marengo County, AL, 67.9% (90% range 56.7–77.4%).
  • 5 of the 50 counties with the highest share of building deductibles of $5,000 or more are in Alabama, which has 39 of the 1,793 listed counties.

Prior work

No ranking of counties or states by the building deductible on record was found in searches on 2026-11-13 (WebSearch: NFIP policies deductible chosen by county; flood insurance deductible choice by county map; NFIP minimum deductible studies). Published work on NFIP deductible choice is national or for one state and does not rank counties:

  • Deductible Choice in Flood Insurance: Who Chooses the Maximum? (Taylor & Francis, 2020; owner-occupied single-family NFIP policies, national, not by county).
  • Michel-Kerjan and Kousky, Come Rain or Shine: Evidence on Flood Insurance Purchases in Florida (Florida policies).

Limitations

  • FEMA records the building deductible on each policy; a deductible on record is not shown to be the owner's choice, and the data does not say who set it or why.
  • Only the building deductible is counted; the contents deductible is separate and not in this measure.
  • This is one snapshot of policies in force on the data date; it shows no change over time.
  • A county's share says nothing about which deductible suits any one home.
  • Counties come from the census geography FEMA codes on each policy (censusGeoid), which can differ from the property's county.
  • Only NFIP records: private flood insurance is not in FEMA's data.
  • A fifth is a position in this list, not a grade, a risk score or a prediction.

Reproduce

Download every record from FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP Policies v3, keep the single-family primary-home policy units with a known building deductible in force on the data date and group them by the county FEMA codes, dropping counties under 30. Compute each share of building deductibles of $5,000 or more with a 90% Wilson interval (z = 1.64485) and check it against the CSV, which gives every numerator and denominator.
